haiku-low.q1: The scheduler's 02:00 UTC trigger starts the run. It extracts replica orders with updated_at greater than HWM minus 2 hours, with no upper bound.
haiku-low.q2: updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time, and bulk imports can hold transactions open up to 90 minutes. A row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at.
haiku-low.q3: The edit bumps updated_at past the HWM, so the next nightly extract (updated_at greater than HWM minus 2 hours) picks it up and the merge updates the row.
haiku-low.q4: The delete arrives as an ordinary update with deleted_at set. The warehouse sets is_deleted to true and never removes the row.
haiku-low.q5: The attempt is marked failed with an error and rolled back, leaving the HWM untouched. The next attempt starts after 15 minutes, up to 3; then on-call is paged.
haiku-low.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed snapshot. The 06:00 freshness check posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts.
haiku-low.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares replica and warehouse counts and checksums for creation days in the last 30 days, and reloads mismatched days.
haiku-low.q8: The stage keeps the newest version per order_id. The MERGE updates only when stage.updated_at is greater than or equal to target.updated_at, so older copies never overwrite newer ones.
haiku-low.q9: It is stored in etl.control as high_water_mark. In step 6, in the same warehouse transaction as the merge, it is set to GREATEST(old HWM, max updated_at of extracted rows).
haiku-low.q10: Step 6 is one warehouse transaction: the MERGE, the HWM advance and the run_log success mark all commit together or roll back together.
haiku-low.q11: The stage is emptied at the start of every attempt, so no leftovers remain. The HWM did not move, so the retry extracts the same window: updated_at greater than HWM minus 2 hours.
haiku-low.q12: It re-reads every order created on each mismatched day from the replica and applies the same guarded MERGE in one transaction. It does not move the nightly HWM.

sonnet.q1: The scheduler's 02:00 UTC trigger starts the orchestrator's nightly run. It extracts all replica `orders` rows with updated_at > (HWM minus 2h), no upper bound.
sonnet.q2: updated_at is stamped at write time, not commit time, and bulk imports can hold a transaction open up to 90 minutes, so a row can become visible up to 90 minutes after its updated_at. The 2h lookback adds 30 minutes for replica lag.
sonnet.q3: The edit bumps updated_at, so the next nightly extract (updated_at > HWM - 2h) picks it up. The guarded MERGE updates the existing warehouse row (stage.updated_at >= target.updated_at).
sonnet.q4: The app sets deleted_at (which also bumps updated_at), so the delete arrives as an ordinary update. The row lands with is_deleted = true (deleted_at IS NOT NULL) and is never removed from the warehouse.
sonnet.q5: It rolls back with HWM untouched, and run_log is marked failed with the error. If fewer than 3 attempts have been made, the orchestrator waits 15 minutes and retries. After the third failure, on-call is paged.
sonnet.q6: Dashboards show the previous committed snapshot. The 06:00 freshness check finds no succeeded nightly run_log row for today and posts a staleness alert to #data-alerts. If the third attempt failed, on-call was also paged earlier.
sonnet.q7: The Sunday reconciliation. It compares per-creation-day row counts and checksums over the last 30 days, finds the mismatched day, re-extracts every row created that day and merges it. The version reaches the warehouse at the next Sunday reconciliation (provided that night's nightly succeeded).
sonnet.q8: The MERGE is guarded: it updates only when stage.updated_at >= target.updated_at. The step 6 query also selects only the newest version per order_id from the stage, so duplicates are removed. An older version can never overwrite a newer one.
sonnet.q9: In the warehouse table etl.control (one row, pipeline='orders', column high_water_mark). It is set to GREATEST(old HWM, max updated_at of the extracted rows) (unchanged if no rows). It is written in step 6, inside the same warehouse transaction as the MERGE and the run_log success mark, at COMMIT.
sonnet.q10: The whole night is loaded in one warehouse transaction (MERGE, HWM advance, run_log success), and dashboards read only committed analytics.orders. Dashboards see the whole night or none of it.
sonnet.q11: The stage is emptied at the start of every attempt, so the retry sees no leftovers. The retry extracts rows with updated_at > HWM - 2h. The HWM did not move on failure, so the window is the same as before.
sonnet.q12: It re-extracts every row created on each mismatched day (by created_at, from the replica) into stage. It applies them with the same guarded MERGE, with all mismatched days in one transaction and the result logged to run_log. It never touches the HWM.
